labels.label: BENIGN
labels.release_path: ShellItemRenderer.cs:393-394 (old page unsubscribed when the displayed page changes); ShellItemRenderer.cs:147-148 in IDisconnectable.Disconnect(), reached from Dispose at ShellItemRenderer.cs:173; ShellRenderer.SetCurrentShellItemControllerAsync calls Disconnect on the old renderer (ShellRenderer.cs:319) and later Dispose (ShellRenderer.cs:339), and also Disconnect+Dispose on a rejected renderer (ShellRenderer.cs:313-314)
labels.teardown_assumption: IDisconnectable.Disconnect or Dispose must run on the ShellItemRenderer; the code shows ShellRenderer calls both when the current shell item renderer is replaced
labels.reason: The same delegate is removed from the same _displayedPage, both when the page changes and in Disconnect. ShellRenderer calls Disconnect/Dispose on the outgoing item renderer, so the teardown path is the one that actually runs. The 'never unsubscribed' text is wrong.

labels.label: BENIGN
labels.release_path: ShellView.cs:236-238 (the old toolbar's IconPressed is removed when a new toolbar is set); there is no Dispose/teardown method in ShellView
labels.teardown_assumption: None runs: ShellView has no teardown. The verdict relies on the toolbar (Shell.Toolbar's platform view, passed in via ViewHandler.Tizen.cs:71-75) being placed inside ShellView's own tree (ShellView.cs:248, _navigationContentView.TitleView) and sharing the Shell's lifetime
labels.reason: The publisher is a MauiToolbar hosted as a child of the subscriber's own view tree, and it comes from the same Shell, so it normally dies with the ShellView. The only case where it outlives an old ShellView is when an app re-creates the Shell handler while keeping the same Shell and toolbar instance; nothing unsubscribes then. That edge case is app-dependent and not a default leak.

labels.label: BENIGN
labels.release_path: CarouselViewController.cs:232-236 DetachingFromWindow -> TearDown(ItemsView) -> CarouselViewController.cs:244 carouselView.Scrolled -= CarouselViewScrolled; triggered by ItemsViewController.cs:192/196-205 (MovedToWindow with Window == null)
labels.teardown_assumption: The iOS MovedToWindow lifecycle event must fire when the collection view leaves the window; the code wires this at ItemsViewController.cs:192, and the platform raises it
labels.reason: Setup (attach to window) and TearDown (detach from window) are symmetric and target the same CarouselView. ItemsView is held through a WeakReference (ItemsViewController.cs:18,21), so the controller does not keep the publisher alive. The CarouselView keeps the controller alive only while the view is in a window, which matches the handler's lifetime. If the handler is disconnected while the view stays in the window, the controller lingers until the view detaches.

The owning ShellSectionRenderer disconnects and disposes this root renderer, so the subscriber is released when its parent is torn down.

labels.label: ACTIONABLE
labels.release_path: WrapperControl.CleanUp() at ViewToHandlerConverter.cs:43-49 removes the handler. It is called only from ShellHeaderView.cs:50-53 and ShellFooterView.cs:53-56 (when the header/footer content is replaced) and from ListViewRenderer.cs:355-361 (on ListView Dispose, only for wrappers still in the visual tree). Nothing cleans up wrappers made by the converter at ViewToHandlerConverter.cs:27 for page TitleView (MauiControlsPageControlStyle.xaml:38) or for ListView containers that were re-templated or recycled
labels.teardown_assumption: CleanUp must be called by the owner of every WrapperControl. For converter-created wrappers (TitleView binding, ListView ContentPresenter rebinding) the code shows no caller, and WrapperControl has no Unloaded or other self-cleanup
labels.reason: Each WrapperControl subscribes to the MAUI View's MeasureInvalidated, and only some creators ever call CleanUp. For a page TitleView, or a ListView cell view that gets re-converted, the old wrapper and its WinUI parent chain stay reachable from the View for as long as that View lives. That matters when an app keeps or shares the TitleView/cell View, so the verdict depends on the app; if the View is discarded too, both are collected together.
